title: Relationships 2.0: How To Keep Conflict From Spiraling

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: No matter how hard we try to avoid them,
sentences.zh: 无论我们多么努力地去避免它们，

sentences.en: conflicts are everywhere.
sentences.zh: 冲突无处不在。

sentences.en: Kids squabble over breakfast at the kitchen table.
sentences.zh: 孩子们在厨房桌子旁为早餐争吵不休。

sentences.en: Colleagues bicker in a team meeting.
sentences.zh: 同事们在团队会议上争执。

sentences.en: Nations clash across the globe.
sentences.zh: 各国在全球范围内发生冲突。

sentences.en: For many of us, our first impulse when it comes to conflict
sentences.zh: 对我们许多人来说，面对冲突时的第一直觉

sentences.en: is to ask, how can I shut it down?
sentences.zh: 就是问：我该如何制止它？

sentences.en: How can I resolve it?
sentences.zh: 我该如何解决它？

sentences.en: This impulse makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这种直觉是有道理的。

sentences.en: Conflict is uncomfortable and unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 冲突是令人感到不舒服和不愉快的。

sentences.en: It produces hurt and animosity.
sentences.zh: 它会产生伤害和敌意。

sentences.en: It can destroy relationships.
sentences.zh: 它会摧毁人际关系。

sentences.en: But sometimes, the roots of antagonism and anger
sentences.zh: 但有时，敌意和愤怒的根源

sentences.en: are so deeply entrenched that avoiding conflict isn't possible
sentences.zh: 根深蒂固，以至于无法避免冲突，

sentences.en: and trying to reach a happy place of agreement and love
sentences.zh: 并且试图达成一个充满赞同与爱的幸福状态

sentences.en: isn't realistic.
sentences.zh: 是不切实际的。

sentences.en: Increasingly, psychological research is taking a different approach
sentences.zh: 越来越多的心理学研究开始对分歧采取一种不同的方法，

sentences.en: to discord with profound implications for disputes big and small.
sentences.zh: 这对大大小小的争端都有着深远的影响。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, we kick off a series
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》中，我们开启了一个系列，

sentences.en: that we're calling Relationships 2.0.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为“关系2.0”。

sentences.en: Today, what if we set aside the goal of eliminating conflict
sentences.zh: 今天，如果我们抛开消除冲突的目标，

sentences.en: and instead ask, how can we do conflict better?
sentences.zh: 转而问：我们该如何更好地处理冲突？

sentences.en: Think back to the last time you found yourself in an argument with someone.
sentences.zh: 回想一下你上次和别人争吵的情形。

sentences.en: It might have been over something trivial,
sentences.zh: 那可能是为了某件琐事，

sentences.en: like a parking spot on a crowded street.
sentences.zh: 比如拥挤街道上的一个停车位。

sentences.en: Or it might have been serious, like the best path forward for a company or a marriage.
sentences.zh: 或者可能是件严肃的事，比如公司或婚姻的最佳前进方向。

sentences.en: Unless you're a very special human being, you likely found yourself getting hot under the collar.
sentences.zh: 除非你是一个非常特别的人，否则你很可能会感到面红耳赤。

sentences.en: You may have felt the other side was being unreasonable, perhaps deliberately so.
sentences.zh: 你可能会觉得对方很不讲理，也许甚至是故意这样的。

sentences.en: At Harvard University, psychologist Julia Minson studies the psychology of disagreement.
sentences.zh: 在哈佛大学，心理学家朱莉娅·明森研究分歧心理学。

sentences.en: In recent years, she has developed some surprisingly simple but powerful techniques
sentences.zh: 近年来，她开发了一些出奇简单但功能强大的技术，

sentences.en: to help people trapped in conflict get unstuck.
sentences.zh: 来帮助陷入冲突无法自拔的人们。

sentences.en: Julia Minson, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅·明森，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Julia, I want to take you back to some of your earliest observations about conflict.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅，我想带你回到你对冲突的一些最早的观察中。

sentences.en: And they took place while you were ballroom dancing,
sentences.zh: 它们发生在你跳交谊舞的时候，

sentences.en: especially when you observed what happened between dancers offstage.
sentences.zh: 尤其是当你观察到舞者在舞台下发生的事情时。

sentences.en: When and where was this?
sentences.zh: 这是什么时候，在哪里？

sentences.en: And what did you observe?
sentences.zh: 你观察到了什么？

sentences.en: So I spent most of my teens and early 20s ballroom dancing,
sentences.zh: 我十几岁到二十出头的大部分时间都在跳交谊舞，

sentences.en: and you just see what happens behind the scenes.
sentences.zh: 你会看到幕后发生的事情。

sentences.en: And what does happen behind the scenes?
sentences.zh: 幕后到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, what happens behind the scenes is, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，幕后发生的事情是，你知道的，

sentences.en: people are practicing and looking like they're fabulously in love.
sentences.zh: 人们在练习，看起来他们正疯狂地相爱着。

sentences.en: And then, you know, the music stops and they break into an argument about,
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，音乐停了，他们开始争论，

sentences.en: well, you know, you were too fast or you were too slow or you were leaning
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道，你太快了，或者你太慢了，或者你在倾斜，

sentences.en: or you were not leaning enough, you know.
sentences.zh: 或者你倾斜得不够，你知道的。

sentences.en: And of course, the other person then doesn't agree with the first person's characterization
sentences.zh: 当然，另一个人随后不同意第一个人对真实情况的描述，

sentences.en: of what really happened, and off they go.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就争论起来了。

sentences.en: So I understand you had a recurrent conflict with your own dance partner, Ryan.
sentences.zh: 据我了解，你和你的舞伴瑞安之间经常发生冲突。

sentences.en: At the time, he was your boyfriend.
sentences.zh: 当时，他是你的男朋友。

sentences.en: He's now your husband.
sentences.zh: 他现在是你的丈夫。

sentences.en: What was that conflict about, Julia?
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅，那场冲突是关于什么的？

sentences.en: You know, so the conflict was something doesn't work, doesn't feel right in the dancing,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，冲突就是有哪里不对劲，跳舞时感觉不对，

sentences.en: and you're looking to diagnose the cause, and the cause is always the other person.
sentences.zh: 你在寻找原因，而原因总是另一个人。

sentences.en: And I started dancing much younger than he did.
sentences.zh: 我开始跳舞的时间比他早得多。

sentences.en: But he is just a more talented dancer.
sentences.zh: 但他是一个更有天赋的舞者。

sentences.en: So between the two of us, I was more knowledgeable, and he was just better.
sentences.zh: 所以在我们俩之间，我懂的理论更多，而他就是跳得更好。

sentences.en: And we are not big screamers.

sentences.en: We are more the silent brooders.
sentences.zh: 我们更倾向于默默生闷气。

sentences.en: But, you know, we've certainly had times where we stop speaking while we're dancing,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我们确实有过在跳舞时停止说话的时候，

sentences.en: but we're preparing for an important competition, so you still have to practice.
sentences.zh: 但我们在准备一场重要的比赛，所以你还得继续练习。

sentences.en: So when you go to graduate school at Stanford University, you started working with the great

sentences.en: I think of naive realism as one of the most important ideas in social psychology,
sentences.zh: 我认为朴素实在论是社会心理学中最核心的思想之一，

sentences.en: and it's basically the idea that people naively believe that their perceptions of reality and
sentences.zh: 它基本上是这样一种观点：人们朴素地相信他们对现实的感知、

sentences.en: how things are and how things ought to be are realistic, right?
sentences.zh: 事物是如何的以及事物应当是如何的，是真实的，对吧？

sentences.en: So what I perceive is what's sort of really out there.
sentences.zh: 所以我所感知的就是真实存在的东西。

sentences.en: Um, and it's an idea that works just fine when we talk about our physical perceptions, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，当我们谈论我们的物理感知时，这个观点运作得很好，对吧？

sentences.en: So if I think something is a solid object, then I should treat it as such and not walk into it.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我认为某物是一个固体对象，那么我就应该把它当作固体对象对待，而不是撞上去。

sentences.en: But then people apply the same conviction to social reality, which is generally really,
sentences.zh: 但随后人们将同样的信念应用到了社会现实中，而社会现实通常非常、非常混乱，

sentences.en: really messy and often hotly contested.
sentences.zh: 并且经常备受争议。

sentences.en: So you take topics where, you know, where reasonable people disagree and see things very,
sentences.zh: 所以你拿一些理性的人们存在分歧、对事情看法截然不同的话题来看，

sentences.en: very differently.
sentences.zh: 他们会把事情看得非常、非常不同。

sentences.en: And yet both sides still think that they have an accurate conceptualization of how reality

sentences.en: really is, right?
sentences.zh: 就像我基本上懂了。

sentences.en: Like I basically get it.

sentences.en: I see how things really are.
sentences.zh: 而人们某种程度上忘记的是，我看到的并不完全是外界真实存在的。

sentences.en: And what people sort of forget is that what I see isn't exactly what's out there.

sentences.en: It's what my brain allows me to see.

sentences.zh: 关于交谊舞，有一件非常奇怪的事情，那就是当你跳舞时，

sentences.zh: 所以当你们绕着房间转，墙上可能有一面镜子时，

sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们希望有一个由竞争对手组成的团队，我们希望有对立的观点，并且每个人

sentences.zh: 真的，当我们谈论普通人的日常生活时，这是关于

sentences.zh: 你认为是什么驱动了这一点？

sentences.zh: 为什么在某些情况下，我们不介意你相信1号球队会赢得超级

sentences.en: you to believe what I believe?
sentences.zh: 你相信我所相信的？

sentences.en: So, I think there's three things that play into it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为有三件事在起作用。

sentences.en: The first factor that, of course, matters is, is this an important issue?
sentences.zh: 当然，重要的第一个因素是：这是一个重要的问题吗？

sentences.en: Is this something that I believe has important consequences?
sentences.zh: 这是我认为会产生重要后果的事情吗？

sentences.en: So, for example, if you and I disagree about the importance of flossing your teeth, it's not
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，如果你和我对用牙线清洁牙齿的重要性有分歧，这并没有

sentences.zh: 重要性有很大的区别。

sentences.en: The second one is what we call interdependence.
sentences.zh: 第二个因素是我们所说的相互依赖性。

sentences.en: So, does your attitude actually affect my outcomes?
sentences.zh: 所以，你的态度真的会影响我的结果吗？

sentences.zh: 如果我们是一对出去吃晚餐的情侣，我想吃中餐而你想吃比萨，我们是完全

sentences.en: interdependent because we have to agree on where we're going.
sentences.zh: 相互依赖的，因为我们必须就去哪里达成一致。

sentences.en: And so, now, if you add that up with importance, your preferences on it directly impact me, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，现在，如果你把这一点和重要性加在一起，你对此的偏好就会直接影响我，对吧？

sentences.en: So, think about, you know, buying a home in this neighborhood or that neighborhood.

sentences.en: It's an important thing and we are stuck together in this house.

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.en: And what's the third factor?
sentences.zh: 那第三个因素是什么？

sentences.en: And basically, what that means is, do I believe that the evidence is overwhelmingly on my side?

sentences.en: And so, once you end up in a situation where the issue is important, we are interdependent in terms of our actions and beliefs,
sentences.zh: 所以，一旦你最终陷入这样一种情况：问题很重要，我们在行动和信念上是相互依赖的，

sentences.en: It's, you know, years of work and we're stuck together because we're co-authors and we both think we have the right answer.

sentences.zh: 正如两方可能会彼此分歧但仍需要共存一样，

sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Julia Minson is a psychologist at the Harvard Kennedy School of Government.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅·明森是哈佛肯尼迪政府学院的一名心理学家。

sentences.en: She studies the psychology of disagreement.
sentences.zh: 她研究分歧心理学。

sentences.en: Many experts in Julia's field of conflict resolution research ways to get people to come to agreement on contentious issues.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅的冲突解决研究领域的许多专家都在寻找方法，让人在有争议的问题上达成一致。

sentences.en: Julia's research has taken a different tack.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅的研究采取了不同的方向。

sentences.en: She has observed that in many cases, people on different sides of a contentious issue might never change their minds,
sentences.zh: 她观察到，在许多情况下，有争议问题不同立场的人可能永远不会改变他们的想法，

sentences.en: but they still need to work together on matters of shared importance.
sentences.zh: 但他们仍然需要在具有共同重要性的事情上进行合作。

sentences.en: Julia, as we've seen, conflicts have a way of spiraling.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅，正如我们所见，冲突往往会不断升级。

sentences.en: Once we jump to the conclusion that people who disagree with us on something are our enemies,
sentences.zh: 一旦我们得出一个结论，即在某事上与我们意见不合的人是我们的敌人，

sentences.en: it poisons the water on every issue, including areas where agreement is possible.
sentences.zh: 这就会毒害每一个问题，包括那些可以达成一致的领域。

sentences.en: Now, you've had a recurring argument with your husband.
sentences.zh: 现在，你和你的丈夫经常发生争执。

sentences.en: Ryan is a data analytics expert, and he periodically wonders whether he should find a new job.
sentences.zh: 瑞安是一位数据分析专家，他定期会考虑自己是否应该找一份新工作。

sentences.en: Tell me how these conversations unfold and how they became a source of conflict.
sentences.zh: 告诉我这些对话是如何展开的，以及它们是如何成为冲突之源的。

sentences.en: Well, so, you know, we have been together for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，你知道的，我们在一起很长时间了。

sentences.en: We've been married for 22 years now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在已经结婚22年了。

sentences.en: So every few years, we go through sort of a period where he says something like,
sentences.zh: 所以每隔几年，我们就会经历一段这样的时期，他说一些类似的话：

sentences.en: well, you know, it's been three years since the last time I've gotten promoted.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，距离我上次晋升已经过去三年了。

sentences.en: And so for the next few months, just FYI, I'm going to be working really long hours because at my next annual review,
sentences.zh: 所以在接下来的几个月里，顺便说一下，我要工作很长时间，因为在我下一次年度考核时，

sentences.en: I want to jump to the next level.
sentences.zh: 我想跃升到下一个级别。

sentences.en: And that all sounds very sensible, but what that really means is that he's going to work really, really hard.
sentences.zh: 这听起来都很明智，但真正意味着的是他将非常、非常努力地工作。

sentences.en: They're not going to recognize it because corporate America is rarely fair.
sentences.zh: 他们不会认可这一点，因为美国企业界很少是公平的。

sentences.en: And then he will be frustrated.
sentences.zh: 然后他会感到沮丧。

sentences.en: And then we'll go through another sort of like long drawn out period of him deciding what to do and whether to move somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 然后我们会经历另一个漫长而拖沓的时期，他决定该做什么以及是否搬到别的地方去。

sentences.en: And, you know.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的。

sentences.en: And you're describing this in a very calm, level-headed, analytical way.
sentences.zh: 你正在以一种非常冷静、理智、分析的方式来描述这一点。

sentences.en: I'm assuming that's the way these conversations actually unfolded?
sentences.zh: 我假设这就是这些对话实际展开的方式吗？

sentences.en: Well, these conversations unfold like this in my head, whereas, you know, in reality, what happens, right,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些对话在我的脑海里是这样展开的，然而，你知道的，现实中发生的是，对吧，

sentences.en: is that he tells me that he's unhappy in his job and I tell him what to do.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我他对工作不满意，而我告诉他该怎么做。

sentences.en: And he says, don't tell me what to do.
sentences.zh: 而他说，别告诉我该怎么做。

sentences.en: And ironically, the longer you're married, the less you feel heard because nobody's actually listening anymore
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，结婚时间越长，你感觉被倾听得越少，因为实际上已经没有人真正在听了，

sentences.en: because we both think we know what the other person is about to say.
sentences.zh: 因为我们都认为自己知道对方接下来要说什么。

sentences.en: He is about to complain about his job.
sentences.zh: 他正要抱怨他的工作。

sentences.en: I'm about to tell him to go get another job offer so that he gets promoted at the current job because he has an alternative offer.
sentences.zh: 我正要告诉他去拿另一份工作offer，这样他就能凭此在当前的工作中获得晋升，因为他有一个替代的offer。

sentences.en: And then he will tell me to stop meddling in his career.
sentences.zh: 然后他会叫我不要干涉他的职业生涯。

sentences.en: And then I will walk off in a huff because it's not just his career.
sentences.zh: 然后我会气冲冲地走开，因为这不仅仅是他的职业生涯。

sentences.en: It's our, you know, whole, it affects the whole family.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的，你知道的，整个人生，它影响着整个家庭。

sentences.en: And, you know, I mean, it's tremendously important.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我的意思是，这极其重要。

sentences.en: You know, my husband's income is the lion's share of the income in our household.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我丈夫的收入是我们家庭收入的大头。

sentences.en: And we are completely interdependent because when he says, I'm going to work much longer hours to get this next promotion,
sentences.zh: 而且我们完全是相互依赖的，因为当他说，我要工作更长时间来争取下一次晋升时，

sentences.en: it means that I am now taking care of three kids with less help.
sentences.zh: 这就意味着我现在要在得不到太多帮助的情况下照顾三个孩子。

sentences.en: And, of course, I teach negotiations, so I think I know how to do this.
sentences.zh: 当然，我教谈判学，所以我认为我知道该怎么做。

sentences.en: So I am 100% confident that I'm right.
sentences.zh: 所以我百分之百确信我是对的。

sentences.en: And he says, no, it's my career in my organization, and I know the rules, and I'm 100% confident that I'm right.
sentences.zh: 而他说，不，这是我在我组织的职业生涯，我知道规则，我百分之百确信我是对的。

sentences.en: Now, you decided to try something with Ryan that you were learning from your research.
sentences.zh: 现在，你决定和瑞安尝试一些你从研究中学到的东西。

sentences.en: But in order to get to that, after your, you know, somewhat false start with that eye contact study,
sentences.zh: 但为了做到这一点，在经历了你对那个眼神接触研究的，你知道的，有点虎头蛇尾的开始之后，

sentences.en: you started working on a technique that you call conversational receptiveness.
sentences.zh: 你开始致力于一项你称之为对话接受度的技术。

sentences.en: What is conversational receptiveness?
sentences.zh: 什么是对话接受度？

sentences.en: So conversational receptiveness is the use of words and phrases to demonstrate to your counterpart that you're engaged with their point of view.
sentences.zh: 因此，对话接受度是使用词语和短语向对方表明你正在倾听他们的观点。

sentences.en: Quite often, when we give people advice about conflict and how they should handle conflict,
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，当我们向人们提供关于冲突以及他们应如何处理冲突的建议时，

sentences.en: we tell them, try to be more empathetic.
sentences.zh: 我们会告诉他们，试着更有同理心。

sentences.en: Try to take the other person's perspective, right?
sentences.zh: 试着站在对方的角度思考，对吧？

sentences.en: Try to exercise intellectual humility.
sentences.zh: 试着表现出智识谦逊。

sentences.en: And what we found was that their counterpart has no idea that they're doing any of that.
sentences.zh: 而我们发现的是，对方根本不知道他们在做这些。

sentences.en: It's not transparent, and because it's not transparent, it has no effect on the conflict.
sentences.zh: 这不是透明的，正因为不透明，它对冲突没有任何影响。

sentences.en: And so conversational receptiveness is basically predicated on the idea that we need to demonstrate to people that were engaged with their point of view
sentences.zh: 因此，对话接受度基本上建立在这样一个理念之上：我们需要以一种对对方来说可见且极易识别的方式向人们表明我们正在倾听他们的观点，

sentences.en: in a way that's visible and very easily recognizable to counterparts because you can't get credit for things in your head.
sentences.zh: 因为你无法为你脑海中的事情获得赞赏。

sentences.en: Julia discovered through her research that there are four specific techniques that communicate conversational receptiveness.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅通过研究发现，有四种具体的技术可以传达对话接受度。

sentences.en: And they make a nice acronym.
sentences.zh: 它们构成了一个很好的缩写词。

sentences.en: The acronym is HEAR, as in I hear you.
sentences.zh: 这个缩写词是HEAR，就像我听到你说的（I hear you）一样。

sentences.en: The H stands for hedging.
sentences.zh: H代表对冲（Hedging）。

sentences.en: So it's saying things like perhaps, or sometimes, or maybe.
sentences.zh: 所以它是说一些诸如“也许”、“有时”或“可能”之类的话。

sentences.en: The E stands for emphasizing agreement.
sentences.zh: E代表强调共识（Emphasizing agreement）。

sentences.en: So I might say, I agree that the last couple years have been really hard on people.
sentences.zh: 所以我可能会说，我同意过去几年对人们来说真的很艰难。

sentences.en: Or we both think that it's really important to make school safe for our kids.
sentences.zh: 或者我们都认为为我们的孩子营造安全的学校环境非常重要。

sentences.en: The A stands for acknowledgement.
sentences.zh: A代表确认（Acknowledgement）。

sentences.en: So it's essentially using some of your own airtime to restate your counterpart's position.
sentences.zh: 所以它本质上是利用你自己的部分发言时间来重申对方的立场。

sentences.en: And then the R stands for reframing to the positive.
sentences.zh: 然后R代表重新构建为积极方向（Reframing to the positive）。

sentences.en: So you can basically say the exact same idea using positive words instead of negative terms, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你基本上可以用积极的词汇而不是消极的词汇来表达完全相同的观点，对吧？

sentences.en: You might say, you know, instead of saying, I hated when people interrupt me,
sentences.zh: 你可能会说，你知道，与其说“我讨厌别人打断我”，

sentences.en: you might say, I really love it when people let me finish.
sentences.zh: 你不如说“我真的很喜欢别人让我把话说完”。

sentences.en: Julia has used this four-step process, hedging, emphasizing areas of agreement,
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅一直使用这四个步骤的过程——对冲、强调共识区域、

sentences.en: acknowledging the other person's perspective, and reframing to the positive
sentences.zh: 确认对方的视角、以及重新构建为积极方向——

sentences.en: to train groups of people in the practice of conversational receptiveness.
sentences.zh: 来训练群体进行对话接受度的练习。

sentences.en: I asked her to describe what happens when people employ these techniques.
sentences.zh: 我请她描述当人们采用这些技术时会发生什么。

sentences.en: So it's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: You know, there is work going back to the 1960s that basically says people love feeling heard.
sentences.zh: 你知道，可以追溯到20世纪60年代的研究基本上表明，人们喜欢被倾听的感觉。

sentences.en: And that's essentially what conversational receptiveness does,
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是对话包容性所起的作用，

sentences.en: is it makes people feel like their counterpart is really engaging with them.
sentences.zh: 也就是让人觉得他们的交流对象真的在倾听并与他们互动。

sentences.en: And so as a consequence, they think of those counterparts as more trustworthy.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们会觉得这些交流对象更值得信赖。

sentences.en: They think of them as being more objective.
sentences.zh: 他们会认为对方更加客观。

sentences.en: They think they have better professional judgment.
sentences.zh: 他们会觉得对方具备更好的专业判断力。

sentences.en: If this is a professional situation, they're more willing to talk to this person about other issues.
sentences.zh: 如果这是一个工作场合，他们会更愿意和这个人讨论其他问题。

sentences.en: So basically you get a lot of positive interpersonal benefits
sentences.zh: 所以基本上你会获得很多积极的人际关系益处，

sentences.en: from essentially saying the same thing,
sentences.zh: 其本质就是说同样的话，

sentences.en: but saying it in a way that acknowledges your partner's point of view.
sentences.zh: 但是用一种承认对方观点的方式表达出来。

sentences.en: And I understand that there are elements of conversational receptiveness that in some ways are contagious,
sentences.zh: 我明白对话包容性中有些元素在某种程度上具有感染力，

sentences.en: that in some ways you're demonstrating it prompts your partner as well to demonstrate some of it?
sentences.zh: 某种程度上来说，当你表现出这种特质时，也会促使你的同伴展现出其中的一部分？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the thing that's very interesting about conversational receptiveness
sentences.zh: 关于对话包容性，非常有趣的一点是，

sentences.en: is that we've done studies where, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们做过这样的研究，你知道的，

sentences.en: we train one person to be conversationally receptive, right?
sentences.zh: 我们训练一个人在对话中表现出包容性，对吧？

sentences.en: Let's say person A, and then person B responds to person A.
sentences.zh: 比方说A，然后B对A做出回应。

sentences.en: And not only is it the case that the more receptive A is, the more receptive B is,
sentences.zh: 不仅A的包容性越强，B的包容性也越强，

sentences.en: but it also seems that B is using other aspects of conversational receptiveness.
sentences.zh: 而且看起来B也在运用对话包容性的其他方面。

sentences.en: So they're picking up kind of like the whole style.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有点像是在模仿整个风格。

sentences.en: They're not just directly copying the words that were said to them.
sentences.zh: 他们不只是直接复制对方向自己说的话。

sentences.en: A lot of the work on conversational receptiveness is focused on the value of asking questions.
sentences.zh: 关于对话包容性的很多研究都聚焦于提问的价值。

sentences.en: And I think most people don't think about the difference between asking questions versus making statements.
sentences.zh: 我想大多数人并没有认真思考过提问与陈述之间的区别。

sentences.en: People don't actually are not conscious when they're having conversations about how many statements
sentences.zh: 人们在对话时，其实并没有意识到自己作出了多少陈述，

sentences.en: they're making versus how many questions they're asking.
sentences.zh: 又提出了多少问题。

sentences.en: But you found that the act of asking questions itself can have a transformative effect on a conversation.
sentences.zh: 但你发现，提问这一行为本身就能对对话产生变革性的影响。

sentences.en: Describe that for me, Julia.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅，能为我描述一下吗？

sentences.en: What it does is it demonstrates curiosity and interest in the other person
sentences.zh: 这样做展现了对另一个人的好奇心和兴趣，

sentences.en: and the desire to learn about them and the desire to sort of show that you're putting in the cognitive effort.
sentences.zh: 以及了解他们的渴望，并且某种程度上表明你付出了认知努力。

sentences.en: And what I mean by that is the very first paper I wrote with Francis when we were at Stanford
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我和弗朗西斯在斯坦福时写的合著的第一篇论文，

sentences.en: and I was still working with Lee Ross was a paper about asking questions.
sentences.zh: 当时我还在和李·罗斯合作，那是一篇关于提问的论文。

sentences.en: And Lee said to us at the time, you know, you are not going to get good results from telling people
sentences.zh: 当时李对我们说，你知道的，如果你告诉人们在冲突中去提问，

sentences.en: to ask questions in conflict because people are going to ask nasty questions.
sentences.zh: 是不会取得好结果的，因为人们会提出刻薄的问题。

sentences.en: They're going to say things like, what kind of idiot believes that?
sentences.zh: 他们会说一些诸如“什么样的大笨蛋才会信这个？”之类的话。

sentences.en: And he was right.
sentences.zh: 他说得对。

sentences.en: So like in most things, having anything to do with psychology, Lee was right.
sentences.zh: 所以就像大多数与心理学相关的事情一样，李是对的。

sentences.en: We only started getting positive sort of effects from question asking when we specified
sentences.zh: 我们只有在明确规定了人们可以问什么类型的问题时，

sentences.en: what kinds of questions people were allowed to ask.
sentences.zh: 才开始从提问中获得积极的效应。

sentences.en: So we call them elaboration questions, which are basically, you know, would you please elaborate?
sentences.zh: 所以我们称之为阐述型问题，基本上就是，你知道的，“能请你详细说说吗？”

sentences.en: So you could say something like, I'm curious why you believe that, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你可以说类似这样的话：“我很想知道你为什么这么认为，”对吧？

sentences.en: It's a statement, but it's doing the work of a question because what it's, you know, it's expressing curiosity.
sentences.zh: 这是一句陈述，但它起到了问题的作，因为它的作用就是表达好奇心。

sentences.en: And that's similar to another paper where we, we got people together who are not in conflict,
sentences.zh: 这类似于我们的另一篇研究，我们把没有发生冲突的人聚集在一起，

sentences.en: people who are simply trying to get to know each other and have sort of a pleasant conversation, right?
sentences.zh: 这些人只是想互相了解，进行一次愉快的对话，对吧？

sentences.en: So imagine, you know, being at a party with colleagues or imagine you're dating, right?
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下，比如和同事在一个派对上，或者想象你在约会，对吧？

sentences.en: What makes for a pleasant conversation?
sentences.zh: 是什么造就了一场愉快的对话？

sentences.en: And what we found was that being asked questions made you like your counterpart more, but it was
sentences.zh: 我们发现，被提问会让你更喜欢你的交流对象，但那是特定类型的问题。

sentences.en: specific questions.
sentences.zh: 那是我们所谓的后续追问。

sentences.en: It was what we called follow-up questions.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我说：“你在哪里长大的？”

sentences.en: So if I said, where did you grow up?
sentences.zh: 而你说芝加哥，我接着就不能说：“你去哪里度假了？”

sentences.en: And you say Chicago, I can't then say, where did you go on vacation?
sentences.zh: 因为虽然这是一个问题，但它忽视了你刚才告诉我的一番话。

sentences.en: Because it's a question, but it's ignoring what you just told me.
sentences.zh: 我最好是说：“哦，你喜欢小熊队吗？”

sentences.en: I would be much better off saying, oh, do you like the Cubs?
sentences.zh: 所以你需要一个能够衔接上下文的问题，因为它表明了你在倾听并且很感兴趣。

sentences.en: So you need a question that follows up because it demonstrates listening and intereSt.
sentences.zh: 其中一些想法可能看起来显而易见。

sentences.en: Some of these ideas might seem obvious.
sentences.zh: 如果你想进行一次愉快的对话，那就去倾听，对对方要说的话表现出兴趣，

sentences.en: If you want to have a good conversation, listen, show interest in what the other person has to say,
sentences.zh: 展现好奇心，避免发表暗示你的观点是唯一值得倾听的观点的陈述。

sentences.en: demonstrate curiosity, avoid making statements that suggest your opinion is the only opinion
sentences.zh: 但知道正确的事情该怎么做与真正做到它们并不是一回事。

sentences.en: worth hearing.
sentences.zh: 但知道正确的事情该怎么做与真正做到它们并不是一回事。

sentences.en: But knowing the right thing to do and actually doing it are not the same thing.
sentences.zh: 有一天下班后，朱莉娅有机会和她的丈夫练习对话包容性。

sentences.en: One day after work, Julia had the opportunity to practice conversational receptiveness with
sentences.zh: 那是一个周五的晚上，朱莉娅在调解研讨会上度过了整整一周，

sentences.en: her husband.
sentences.zh: 在那里她得以练习对话包容性的艺术。

sentences.en: It was on a Friday evening, and Julia had spent the entire week at a mediation seminar where
sentences.zh: 这是连续五天、每天八小时纯粹的调解训练。

sentences.en: she got to practice the art of conversational receptiveness.
sentences.zh: 调解员使用的一个重要技术被称为“倾听三角”，

sentences.en: This was five days, eight hours a day of nothing but mediation.
sentences.zh: 这与对话包容性在概念上密切相关。

sentences.en: And an important technique that mediators use is something they call the listening triangle,
sentences.zh: 你向处于冲突中的一方提出一个问题。

sentences.en: which is very conceptually related to conversational receptiveness.
sentences.zh: 你倾听他们的回答。

sentences.en: You ask a party in conflict a question.
sentences.zh: 然后你说：“嗯，我刚刚听到你说的是甲、乙、丙。”

sentences.en: You listen to the answer.
sentences.zh: “是这样吗？”

sentences.en: And then you say, well, I just heard you say X, Y, Z.
sentences.zh: 接着这就开启了下一轮对话，因为你刚刚提出了一个问题。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 所以现在你必须倾听对方的回答。

sentences.en: And then that starts the next round because you just asked a question.
sentences.zh: 然后他们说完了。

sentences.en: And so now you have to listen to the answer.
sentences.zh: 你说：“啊哈，所以听起来你是在说巴拉巴拉巴拉。”

sentences.en: And then they finish talking.
sentences.zh: “是这样吗？”

sentences.en: And you say, aha, so it seems like you're saying blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 然后你就这样无休止地重复下去，直到你倾听的那个人说：“对，对，对，你抓住了重点。”

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: “行了，我说完了。”

sentences.en: And then you're just supposed to do this endlessly until the person you're listening to says, yeah,
sentences.zh: 我对这项技术印象深刻。

sentences.en: yeah, yeah, you got it.
sentences.zh: 我原以为这真的与对话包容性有关，因为这一切都建立在认可的基础上。

sentences.en: Like, I'm done.
sentences.zh: 然后，你懂的，一周的时间结束了，到了周五晚上。

sentences.en: And I was impressed with this technique.
sentences.zh: 我记得我们在厨房的吧台喝着马提尼。

sentences.en: And I thought that this was really related to conversational receptiveness because it's
sentences.zh: 我丈夫说起了他有时候会说的那种话，你知道的，“我要非常努力地工作，

sentences.en: all based on acknowledgement.
sentences.zh: 因为有些项目我想完成，我想获得晋升”，

sentences.en: And then, you know, the week runs out and it's Friday night.
sentences.zh: 我甚至都没多想就脱口而出：“你总是这么说，然后什么都不做，最后也什么功劳都捞不到。”

sentences.en: And I remember having martinis at our kitchen bar.
sentences.zh: “接下来你应该这么做。”

sentences.en: And my husband says the thing that he, you know, sometimes says that, you know, I'm going
sentences.zh: 他听完后非常、非常生我的气。

sentences.en: to be working really hard because there are these projects I want to finish and I want to get
sentences.zh: 我有点惊讶他会这么生气。

sentences.en: promoted and without giving it another thought, I said, you always say this and then you never do
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我们在这次对话刚开始时谈到的那样，我们不是那种大吵大闹的人，

sentences.en: anything about it and then you never get credit for it.
sentences.zh: 我们是那种会在心里默默生闷气的人。

sentences.en: And here's what you should do instead.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，你看，他在默默地洗碗，而我坐在厨房吧台旁喝着马提尼，

sentences.en: And he was so, so upset with me.
sentences.zh: 这美好的夜晚就这么，你知道的，给毁了。

sentences.en: And I was sort of surprised by how upset he was.
sentences.zh: 我试图弄清楚刚才究竟发生了什么，以及我们是怎么走到这一步的。

sentences.en: And as I said, when we're talking in the beginning of this conversation, we're not yellers,
sentences.zh: 然后我想起了我一整周都在上的该死的课。

sentences.en: we're slow brooders.
sentences.zh: 这种讽刺感让我震惊，因为我明明清楚地知道自己本该怎么做。

sentences.en: So now, you know, he is silently washing the dishes and I'm sitting there at the kitchen
sentences.zh: 我从自己的研究中深知这一点，而且我刚刚花了一周时间在陌生人身上练习它。

sentences.en: bar with this martini that, you know, the nice evening just kind of, you know, got destroyed.
sentences.zh: 然后我恰好处于一个完美适用该技术的时刻，却根本没想到要去运用它。

sentences.en: And I'm trying to understand what just happened and how we got here.
sentences.zh: 因此我感到很惊讶，要在当下那一刻把这些知识调动出来竟然这么难。

sentences.en: And then I remember this damn class I've been in all week.
sentences.zh: 而且一旦它浮现在我的脑海中，要真正付诸实践又是何等艰难。

sentences.en: And the irony just blew my mind that I knew exactly what I should have done.
sentences.zh: 朱莉娅，你当时做了什么？

sentences.en: And I knew it from my research and I had just spent a week practicing it on strangers.
sentences.zh: 我在那儿坐了大概，我不知道，15、20分钟，一直在进行激烈的内心挣扎。

sentences.en: And then I was in this moment when it was perfectly applicable and I didn't even think of doing it.
sentences.zh: 然后我真的就开口说：“你知道吗，我们再试一次。”

sentences.en: And so I was surprised at how hard it was to, one, even bring that knowledge online in the moment.
sentences.zh: “告诉我为什么你觉得自己需要更努力、工作更长时间。”

sentences.en: And then once it was kind of top of mind for me to really execute on it.
sentences.zh: 接着我真的就闭上嘴巴开始倾听，并提出了后续的追问。

sentences.en: What did you do, Julia?
sentences.zh: 我其实一点都不是真心感兴趣，对吧？

sentences.en: I sat there for probably, I don't know, 15, 20 minutes wrestling with myself.
sentences.zh: 我只是想化解一场争吵。

sentences.en: And then I literally just said, you know what, let's try this again.
sentences.zh: 他虽然对我谈不上满意，但这确实起到了作用。

sentences.en: Tell me why you think you need to work harder and longer.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他并不是在寻求我对他的职业生涯提出意见。

sentences.en: And then I just like shut my mouth and I listened and I asked follow-up questions.
sentences.zh: 他只是在我支持他去做他认为必须做的事情时，希望得到我的支持。

sentences.en: And I was very much not like genuinely interested, right?
sentences.zh: 而我坐在那里，脑子里一直在想：他到底什么时候才会来征求我的意见？

sentences.en: I was just trying to diffuse a fight.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，但我对自己说：“不，算了。”

sentences.en: And he wasn't like happy with me, but it did do the job.
sentences.zh: 我对自我说：“我再也不那样做了。”

sentences.en: And he was actually not looking for my input in his career.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是不断提问、澄清，然后，你知道的，他就开始滔滔不绝。

sentences.en: He was looking for my support while he did what he thought needed to be done.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，他开始主动说：“嗯，你觉得我该怎么做？”

sentences.en: And the entire time I'm sitting there thinking in my head, when is he going to ask me for my opinion?
sentences.zh: 然后我才非常小心翼翼地说：“嗯，我可能会考虑做甲、乙、丙，对吧？”

sentences.en: You know, but I'm like, nope.
sentences.zh: 也就是有点像在缓和我的主张，只是把它作为一个建议提出来，而不是说“你必须去这么做”。

sentences.en: I said to myself, I'm not doing that anymore.
sentences.zh: 这种动态关系一直延续到现在，那就是认识到这是他自己的职业生涯。

sentences.en: And so I would just ask questions and clarify and, you know, and he would talk.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我给予了他这种尊重，反过来也让他给予了我尊重，对我说：“嘿，谈判专家，我该怎么做？”

sentences.en: And then over time, he started saying, well, what do you think I should do?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这里面有一个莫大的讽刺，不是吗？

sentences.en: And I started very carefully saying, well, I might consider possibly doing X, Y, Z, right?
sentences.zh: 那就是你逼得越紧，他反而越固执己见，并且停止倾听。

sentences.en: Which is sort of hedging my claims and just sort of offering it as a suggestion, not saying you need to go do X.
sentences.zh: 但当你停止施压并开始倾听时，不仅能让你减少愤怒，他突然也会觉得找你倾诉和征求你的建议变得容易多了。

sentences.en: And that's sort of been the dynamic is recognizing that it is his career.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I think me giving him that respect has led him to give me the respect of saying, hey, negotiation professor, what should I do?
sentences.zh: 这也是我们研究中的发现。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a real irony here, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我们在研究对话包容性时，其中一项研究实际上是为了看看表现出包容性是否会让你显得不那么有说服力，对吧？

sentences.en: Which is the harder you push, the more he digs in his heels and stops listening.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象，如果你在言论中留有余地、表现出赞同并让对方多说话，这可能会被视为你很不确定。

sentences.en: But when you stop pushing and start listening, it not only makes you less angry, but he suddenly finds it easier to seek you out and ask you for your advice.

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 但相反，我们发现了截然不同的结果。

sentences.en: And that's their findings in our research as well.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当面对在敏感话题上意见不合的人时，对吧？

sentences.en: So one of the studies we did with conversational receptiveness was actually to see whether being receptive might make you less persuasive, right?
sentences.zh: 比如“黑人的命也是命”运动，或者大学在校园发生性侵指控时应该采取什么行动。

sentences.en: So you could imagine if you're hedging your claims and showing agreement and letting the other person talk, it might be seen as like you're uncertain.
sentences.zh: 当你训练其中一方使用对话包容性时，另一方实际上更有可能稍微向他们的立场靠拢。

sentences.en: And so your message actually has less impact.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨对话包容性的障碍以及如何克服它们。

sentences.en: But instead, we found the opposite.
sentences.zh: 您正在收听的是《隐蔽的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: We found that when you have people who disagree on hot button issues, right?
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.en: So like Black Lives Matter or, you know, what universities should do when there's an accusation of sexual assault on campus.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐蔽的大脑》。

sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.zh: 你最近在没日没夜地筹备一个大型学术会议时，就和一位同事发生了冲突。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲发生了什么事。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我们和一位为会议组织小组讨论的研究人员沟通失误了，那个小组讨论没有出现在日程表上，然后，你知道的，

sentences.en: Psychologist Julia Minson studies how conversational receptiveness can diffuse conflicts and allow people to work together even in the face of intractable disagreements.
sentences.zh: 那位研究人员很不高兴。

sentences.en: Julia, the behaviors associated with conversational receptiveness seem relatively straightforward, and yet they can be difficult to implement, as you yourself have discovered.
sentences.zh: 我们收到了一封回复邮件，上面写着：“让我告诉你，作为一个有色人种女性，我的角色不被认真对待，我是多么的厌烦和疲惫。”

sentences.en: You recently had a conflict with a colleague as you were working around the clock to organize a huge academic conference.
sentences.zh: 这封邮件中有几点，你知道的，让我特别难过。

sentences.en: Tell me what happened.
sentences.zh: 其中一点是，组织这个会议根本不在我的职责范围之内。

sentences.en: We had a miscommunication with one of the researchers who had organized a panel for the conference, and the panel did not appear on the schedule, and, you know,
sentences.zh: 在这个每个人都在Zoom上四处奔波、极力维持工作运转的大危机时期，我是在帮整个学术界一个忙。

sentences.en: the researcher was upset.
sentences.zh: 所以我接下了这个重任，会议临近，每个人都在非常、非常努力地工作。

sentences.en: And we got an email back that said, let me tell you how sick and tired I am as a woman of color not being taken seriously in my role.
sentences.zh: 当然，另一个让我感到特别毫无根据的指控是，我们因为她是女性有色人种而虐待她，因为，你知道的，

sentences.en: And there were a couple things that, you know, made me particularly upset about this email.
sentences.zh: 她没有被列入日程表完全是一个误会，而且是一个无心的误会。

sentences.en: One was that organizing this conference is sort of nowhere in my job description.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时真的很沮丧，对吧？

sentences.en: I was doing the field a favor during kind of this big time of crisis where, you know, everybody was running around trying to keep work afloat on Zoom.
sentences.zh: 我当时在杂货店，字面意义上正站在蔬果区，突然就收到了这样一封邮件，一口咬定我既是个种族主义者又是个性别歧视者。

sentences.en: And so I had taken on this big task, and we were rapidly approaching the conference, and everybody was working really, really hard.
sentences.zh: 我感觉自己在这一周的大部分时间里都像是在经历一场危机。

sentences.en: And the other piece, of course, is the accusation that we, you know, mistreated this person because she is a woman of color felt particularly unfounded because, you know,
sentences.zh: 我以为我已经处理好了那场危机。

sentences.en: them being left off the program was a complete misunderstanding and an innocent one of that.
sentences.zh: 然后邮件又雪上加霜。

sentences.en: And so I was really upset, right?
sentences.zh: 当时我真的感到非常无助。

sentences.en: I'm at the grocery store, like literally in the produce aisle, and I get this email that's accusing me of being a racist and a sexist in one breath.
sentences.zh: 那真是一个让人透不过气的时刻。

sentences.en: And I've sort of at this point learned my lessons about conversational receptiveness, and I thought, okay, here's what I need to do.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，我已经吸取了关于对话接受度的教训，我想，好吧，这就是我需要做的。

sentences.en: I need to get home, and I need to write this email, and I'm going to use conversational receptiveness, and I'm going to acknowledge, and I'm going to hedge my claims,
sentences.zh: 我得回家，我得写这封电子邮件，我要运用对话接受度的技巧，我要表示认可，我要留有余地，

sentences.en: and I'm going to find areas of agreement and all the things.
sentences.zh: 我要寻找共鸣点以及所有这些东西。

sentences.en: And the entire time I'm driving home, and I'm writing these different drafts of this email in my head, and none of them sound receptive.
sentences.zh: 在我开车回家的整个过程中，我一直在脑子里写这封邮件的不同草稿，但没有一个听起来是具有接受态度的。

sentences.en: All of them are focused on me wanting to express how incredibly upset I am that this happened to me, and how right I am, and how wrong she is,
sentences.zh: 它们全都集中在我想要表达这件事情发生在我身上是多么令人难以置信的沮丧，我是多么正确，她是多么错误，

sentences.en: and how underappreciated and frustrated I am.
sentences.zh: 以及我是多么不被赏识和沮丧。

sentences.en: And, I mean, honestly, by the time I was coming home, I was starting to think, like, well, maybe conversational receptiveness isn't that useful,
sentences.zh: 而且，说实话，当我回到家的时候，我开始觉得，嗯，也许对话接受度并没有那么有用，

sentences.en: because I can't think of any way to apply it to the situation.
sentences.zh: 因为我想不出任何方法把它应用到这种情况下。

sentences.en: You know, and then I walk in the house, and my husband starts helping me unload the groceries, and I'm telling him about this whole thing, and I'm, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，然后我走进屋子，我丈夫开始帮我卸杂货，我正跟他讲这整件事，你知道的，

sentences.en: fuming and saying how I need to write back, because I can't just, like, ignore this.
sentences.zh: 我气冲冲地，说我必须回信，因为我不能就这么无视它。

sentences.en: But also, I can't think of anything particularly civil to say, and he basically just started dictating the email to me, because, you know, of course,
sentences.zh: 但同时，我又想不出什么特别客气的话来，然后他基本上就开始帮我口述这封邮件，因为，你知道的，当然，

sentences.en: he listens to me talk about conversational receptiveness all day long.
sentences.zh: 他整天听我谈论对话接受度。

sentences.en: So he knows the entire toolkit, and he was just fabulous at it, and, I mean, I literally typed out what he said, and I sent it off, and within hours,
sentences.zh: 所以他了解整套方法，而且他在这方面表现得太棒了，我的意思是，我 literalmente 照着他说的话打字，然后发了出去，几个小时之内，

sentences.en: I got a lovely email back that said,
sentences.zh: 我收到了一封可爱的回信，上面写着，

sentences.en: Thank you so much for understanding, and you can relate to how hard it is to be a woman in academia, and, you know, one day when, you know, the pandemic is over,
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您的理解，您能体会到作为一个学术界的女性是多么艰难，而且，你知道的，等到哪天疫情结束了，

sentences.en: we will get together, and we'll get to know each other, and it was just a very nice email from a person who felt heard.
sentences.zh: 我们会聚在一起，我们会互相了解，这真是一封来自一个觉得自己被倾听的人的非常好的邮件。

sentences.en: And, I mean, my husband gets the credit for hearing her, because in that moment, I certainly couldn't.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，我丈夫应该因为倾听了她而受到赞扬，因为在那一刻，我绝对做不到。

sentences.en: So I want to talk about the role of emotions as we're having these conflicts and disagreements.
sentences.zh: 所以我想讨论一下当我们陷入这些冲突和分歧时，情绪所起的作用。

sentences.en: It's hard in the middle of a heated argument to put on your thinking cap and remember what the smart thing is to do.
sentences.zh: 在激烈的争论中，你很难保持理智，记住什么才是明智的做法。

sentences.en: Can you just talk about how our emotions can sidetrack us from what is self-evidently the right thing to do?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈我们的情绪是如何让我们偏离显而易见的正确做法的吗？

sentences.en: It's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: Emotion, of course, plays a huge role in conflict.
sentences.zh: 当然，情绪在冲突中起着巨大的作用。

sentences.en: And in some of my work, what we see is that, you know, the primary emotion in attitude conflict is anger.
sentences.zh: 在我的一些研究中，我们发现，在观点冲突中，主要的情绪是愤怒。

sentences.en: It's anger and frustration, sort of why don't these people get it?
sentences.zh: 是愤怒和沮丧，有点像这些人为什么不明白？

sentences.en: Why don't they see it the way I see it?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们看不到我所看到的东西？

sentences.en: So I think anger and frustration play a huge role in our inability to sort of do the right thing, even when you know what the right thing is.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为愤怒和沮丧在我们无法做出正确行为方面起着巨大的作用，即使你知道什么是正确的事。

sentences.en: You know, it's like there's like I almost think of like there's a bug flying and I just have to like smush it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就像，我甚至觉得就像有只苍蝇在飞，我只想把它拍死。

sentences.en: You know, I can't let it keep flying around my head.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不能让它一直在我的头顶飞来飞去。

sentences.en: And it's that impulse to put an end to the speech that you strongly disagree with, I think often gets us in trouble.
sentences.zh: 正是这种想要结束你强烈反对的言论的冲动，我认为往往会给我们带来麻烦。

sentences.en: One thing that you have found that poisons the water and in some ways, you know, the letter that you received from your fellow academic, I think, speaks to this,
sentences.zh: 你发现的一件会毒化气氛的事情——在某种程度上，你知道，你从同行学者那里收到的信，我认为就说明了这一点——

sentences.en: is that when we're upset in conflicts, many of us resort to using moral language.
sentences.zh: 那就是当我们在冲突中感到沮丧时，我们许多人都会诉诸道德语言。

sentences.en: So I don't just simply say, you know, I'm upset that I've been left off the conference schedule.
sentences.zh: 所以我不仅仅是说，你知道的，我对于自己被排在会议日程之外感到很不满。

sentences.en: What explains the oversight?
sentences.zh: 是什么导致了这种疏忽？

sentences.en: The person went to the additional length of basically saying I've been left off the conference schedule because of racism and sexism.
sentences.zh: 这个人还进一步表示，我被排除在会议日程之外是因为种族主义和性别歧视。

sentences.en: What is the effect of using moralizing language as we are debating and disagreeing with each other, Julia?
sentences.zh: 朱莉，在我们互相辩论和分歧时，使用道德化的语言会有什么影响？

sentences.en: Yeah, so moralizing language tends to pour oil on the fire in the sense that it's very, very hard to stand in the face of that kind of accusation and not react emotionally, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，所以道德化的语言往往会火上浇油，因为面对这种指控而不做出情绪化的反应是非常非常难的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And of course, in the course of arguments, we often think that using moral language is sort of a sledgehammer, right?
sentences.zh: 当然，在争论的过程中，我们经常认为使用道德语言就像是一种大锤，对吧？

sentences.en: It's sort of where we use it almost as a tactical weapon on the battlefield to basically disarm and disable our opponents.
sentences.zh: 它有点像我们在战场上作为战术武器使用，基本上是为了解除对手的武装和战斗力。

sentences.en: But of course, our opponents are doing exactly the same to us.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我们的对手也在对我们做完全相同的事情。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: And this is sort of, you know, back to naive realism, right?
sentences.zh: 这有点像，你知道的，回到朴素现实主义，对吧？

sentences.en: We believe that we have the ultimate kind of form of evidence on our side, which is that our argument is morally superior.
sentences.zh: 我们相信我们这一边拥有终极形式的证据，那就是我们的论点在道德上更占优势。

sentences.en: And so once I bring that, you know, moral perspective into this, there's no longer going to be any debate.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦我把这种道德视角带入其中，就不会再有任何辩论了。

sentences.en: One of the things about this four-stage process that you articulated, one of the more surprising things, I think,
sentences.zh: 关于你阐述的这个四个阶段的过程，其中一个更令人惊讶的事情，我想，

sentences.en: is that you find that when people spend time articulating their opponent's point of view,
sentences.zh: 那就是你发现，当人们花时间阐述对手的观点时，

sentences.en: actually giving their own airtime to articulating what their opponents think, it actually makes it more likely that they are going to be heard in turn.
sentences.zh: 实际上是把他们自己的谈话时间让出来阐述对手的想法，这实际上会让他们更有可能反过来被倾听。

sentences.en: And why do you think that it's effective to spend your own airtime articulating what the other person is thinking?
sentences.zh: 你认为花出自己的时间去阐述对方的想法为什么是有效的？

sentences.en: I think there's probably two reasons why it works.
sentences.zh: 我想这行之有效可能有两个原因。

sentences.en: I spend a lot of time thinking about why is it we're in such a rush in conflict.
sentences.zh: 我花了很多时间思考为什么我们在冲突中会如此急躁。

sentences.en: And I think there's two reasons why we're in a rush.
sentences.zh: 我想我们急躁有两个原因。

sentences.en: One is how it just feels terrible to have, you know, bad ideas out in the world and how we just want to like bat them down.
sentences.zh: 一个是世界上存在糟糕的想法会让人感觉糟糕透顶，而我们只想把它们击垮。

sentences.en: The other is that most of these conversations are very unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 另一个原因是其中大多数对话都非常令人不快。

sentences.en: And so you want to get out of there and you expect that your partner wants to get out of there.
sentences.zh: 所以你想离开那里，而且你预料你的伴侣也想离开那里。

sentences.en: And so there's this feeling of like, if I don't say it, then I'm never going to have a chance to say it because this is going to be, you know, a short and furious conversation.
sentences.zh: 因此会有一种感觉：如果我现在不说，那我以后就再也没有机会说了，因为这将是一场短暂而激烈的对话。

sentences.en: I think acknowledging your counterpart's point of view and really listening to them and asking them lots of questions triggers two things.
sentences.zh: 我认为承认对方的观点并真正倾听他们，问他们很多问题会触发两件事。

sentences.en: One, it triggers reciprocity, right?
sentences.zh: 第一，它会触发互惠心理，对吧？

sentences.en: So reciprocity is one of the most powerful social forces we've ever studied.
sentences.zh: 所以互惠是我们研究过的最强大的社会力量之一。

sentences.en: And if I listen to you patiently and at length, and then I start talking, you're going to feel like a real jerk interrupting me.
sentences.zh: 如果我耐心且长时间地听你说话，然后我开始说话，你会觉得自己打断我是一个十足的混蛋。

sentences.en: And now that I have given you my time and, you know, lent you my ear, you now have to do the same.
sentences.zh: 既然我已经把我的时间和倾听给了你，你现在也必须这样做。

sentences.en: And I think the second thing it triggers is it makes the conversation much less unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 我认为它触发的第二件事是，它让对话变得不那么令人不快。

sentences.en: And therefore, that feeling of urgency disappears, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，那种紧迫感就消失了，对吧？

sentences.en: We go from this, like, how fast can I say my piece because this is all about to explode to let's have a long, thoughtful,
sentences.zh: 我们从这种“我必须以最快速度说出我的观点，因为这一切都快要爆发了”的状态，转变为进行一场漫长、深思熟虑、

sentences.en: drawn out conversation about this that just has a very different pace to it.
sentences.zh: 拉长了的对话，它的节奏完全不同。

sentences.en: In studying conversational receptiveness, you drew a distinction between actually displaying conversational receptiveness as in actually feeling it, you know,
sentences.zh: 在研究对话接受度时，你区分了实际表现出对话接受度（就像真实感受到它一样，你知道，

sentences.en: what's going on inside your head, and actually demonstrating it on the outside, regardless of whether you actually feel that way or not.
sentences.zh: 你脑子里在想什么）和在表面上表现出来，而不管你实际上是不是这种感觉。

sentences.en: So in the email that you composed to your fellow academic, presumably at the point at which you hit send, given that your husband composed the email for you, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以在你写给同行学者的那封电子邮件中，据推测在你点击发送的那一刻，鉴于这封邮件是你丈夫为你写的，你知道，

sentences.en: you didn't actually feel everything that you said in the email.
sentences.zh: 你实际上并没有感受到邮件中所说的一切。

sentences.en: And yet it had the effect of having the other person say, okay, this person is really listening to me.
sentences.zh: 然而它却起到了让对方说“好吧，这个人确实在听我说话”的效果。

sentences.en: What are you recommending here?
sentences.zh: 你在这里的建议是什么？

sentences.en: Are you recommending that we actually try to be more empathetic and open to other people or that we simply just demonstrate that we're doing those things?
sentences.zh: 你是建议我们真正努力变得更有同理心、对他人更开放，还是仅仅表现出我们在做这些事情？

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: I wish the world was a place where people in conflict could feel empathetic and open and then act on that empathy in a way that's sort of transparent and recognizable to their counterparts.
sentences.zh: 我希望世界是一个这样的地方：处于冲突中的人们可以感受到同理心和开放，然后以一种对他们的对手来说透明且可识别的方式将这种同理心付诸行动。

sentences.en: But I don't think that's how humans work.
sentences.zh: 但我不认为人类是这样运作的。

sentences.en: I think conversational receptiveness is a lot like the other types of aspirations we have that sometimes we live up to and sometimes we fail to live up to, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为对话接受度很像我们拥有的其他类型的抱负，有时我们能做到，有时我们做不到，对吧？

sentences.en: So we have lots of goals.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有很多目标。

sentences.en: I want to exercise more often.
sentences.zh: 我想更频繁地锻炼。

sentences.en: I want to spend less time on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 我想减少刷推特的时间。

sentences.en: You know, I want to, you know, call my mom, like all the things that you know you want to do, but for various reasons you fail to live up to.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想，你知道，给我妈妈打电话，就像所有那些你知道你想做但出于各种原因没能做到的事情一样。

sentences.en: And I think conversational receptiveness is like that.
sentences.zh: 我认为对话接受度就是这样的。

sentences.en: It's that you aren't as receptive as you aspire to be.
sentences.zh: 也就是你并没有你想象的那么具有接受度。

sentences.en: And so in that moment, I think faking it is perfectly fine, right?
sentences.zh: 所以在那个时刻，我认为假装一下完全没问题，对吧？

sentences.en: You get there however you get there because it leads to a better outcome.
sentences.zh: 不管你用什么方法达到目的，只要它能带来更好的结果就行。

sentences.en: You know, if you think back to my example, right, I didn't write the email that the screaming voice in my head was writing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，回想一下我的例子，对吧？我并没有写出我脑海中那个尖叫的声音在写的邮件。

sentences.en: I knew that that was not the kind of person I wanted to be in this situation.
sentences.zh: 我知道那不是我想在这种情况下成为的那种人。

sentences.en: And so I think conversational receptiveness is a toolkit to kind of help people live up to their best selves,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为对话接受度是一套工具，可以帮助人们展现出他们最好的一面，

sentences.en: even when in the emotional moment they can't quite do it like they can't improvise their way there.
sentences.zh: 即使在情绪化的时刻他们无法完全做到这一点，就像他们无法即兴做到那样。

sentences.en: Or they can't do it authentically, if you will.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你愿意的话，他们无法真实地做到这一点。

sentences.en: Right, right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: But the diffused fight is better than the undiffused fight.
sentences.zh: 但是，化解了的争吵总比没有化解的争吵要好。

sentences.en: Conversational receptiveness is not a magic bullet.
sentences.zh: 对话接受度并不是万灵药。

sentences.en: Not everyone you listen to carefully is going to come around to your point of view.
sentences.zh: 并不是每一个你仔细倾听的人都会转而支持你的观点。

sentences.en: In her own life,
sentences.zh: 在她的生活中，

sentences.en: Julia has realized that what conversational receptiveness really allows her to do is to keep an intractable conflict in one domain from derailing an entire relationship.
sentences.zh: 朱莉已经意识到，对话接受度真正让她能够做到的是，防止一个领域中无法调和的冲突破坏整段关系。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think part of what happens is people are so focused on persuading the other side that they don't think about laying the groundwork for the next conversation, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为发生的一部分情况是，人们太专注于说服对方，以至于他们没有考虑为下一次对话打下基础，对吧？

sentences.en: Every conversation is just the lead up to the future conversation.
sentences.zh: 每一次对话都只是通往未来对话的铺垫。

sentences.en: And so what can you do now to make the next one better, kinder, more informative, more harmonious, you know, all of those things.
sentences.zh: 那么你现在能做什么来让下一次对话更好、更温和、更有信息量、更和谐，你知道，所有这些。

sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，说服可能会也可能不会在某个过程中发生，但我们能否专注于下一次对话？

sentences.en: Our story comes from Rich Addison.
sentences.zh: 我们的故事来自里奇·埃迪森。

sentences.en: So when I was young, I was very shy.
sentences.zh: 所以当我年轻的时候，我非常害羞。

sentences.en: I was an only child who was pretty comfortable talking to adults, but I never had any brothers and sisters to practice on.
sentences.zh: 我是个独生子女，跟成年人说话挺自在的，但我从来没有兄弟姐妹可以用来练习。

sentences.en: So I wasn't very good at kind of mixing it up with the other kids.
sentences.zh: 所以我不太擅长跟其他小孩子打成一片。

sentences.en: And I remember being very anxious about going to school.
sentences.zh: 我记得我对去上学感到非常焦虑。

sentences.en: And on Sunday nights, I would not be able to sleep, just worrying about what would happen with the other kids.
sentences.zh: 每到周日晚上，我都睡不着觉，整天担心和其他小孩子在一起会发生什么。

sentences.en: So now, flash forward a few years, and I'm in high school.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，快进几年，我上高中了。

sentences.en: And I realized that I had to be different, that I couldn't keep being so shy.
sentences.zh: 我意识到我必须有所改变，我不能一直这么害羞下去。

sentences.en: So I went about developing a quick wit and a sense of humor that would keep other kids off balance, so I wouldn't have to feel powerless.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始培养一种机智和幽默感，好让其他小孩子不知所措，这样我就不用感到无能为力了。

sentences.en: You know how sometimes people say the best defense is a good offense?
sentences.zh: 你知道有时人们说最好的防御就是进攻吗？

sentences.en: Well, that was what I was doing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是我当时在做的。

sentences.en: But the sense of humor I developed was kind of biting and kind of critical.
sentences.zh: 但我培养出的幽默感有点刻薄，也爱挑剔。

sentences.en: So now, my hero is about to come into the story.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，我的主人公要登场了。

sentences.en: And this was my friend Holly.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的朋友霍莉。

sentences.en: And one day, Holly and I were talking, and she said to me,
sentences.zh: 有一天，我和霍莉在聊天，她对我说，

sentences.en: You know, Rich, sometimes you really hurt people's feelings.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，里奇，有时你真的会伤害别人的感情。

sentences.en: And at first, I was just shocked.
sentences.zh: 起初，我简直惊呆了。

sentences.en: I said to myself, That can't be true.
sentences.zh: 我对自己说，这不可能是真的。

sentences.en: I was entertaining.
sentences.zh: 我很有趣。

sentences.en: I made people laugh.
sentences.zh: 我逗大家笑。

sentences.en: I liked people.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢人们。

sentences.en: These were my friends.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我的朋友。

sentences.en: I didn't want to hurt them.
sentences.zh: 我不想伤害他们。

sentences.en: I couldn't be hurting them.
sentences.zh: 我不可能在伤害他们。

sentences.en: But I kept thinking about what Holly said, and I kept turning it over in my mind.
sentences.zh: 但我一直在想霍莉的话，我在脑海里反复琢磨。

sentences.en: And eventually, I realized that she was absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 最终，我意识到她绝对是对的。

sentences.en: And I started paying attention to how my humor was affecting other people.
sentences.zh: 我开始注意我的幽默是如何影响其他人的。

sentences.en: And I changed it.
sentences.zh: 我改变了。

sentences.en: It didn't happen immediately.
sentences.zh: 这不是马上发生的。

sentences.en: It didn't happen overnight.
sentences.zh: 这不是一夜之间发生的。

sentences.en: But I changed, and I wanted to be more compassionate towards people.
sentences.zh: 但我改变了，我想对人们多一些同情心。

sentences.en: And I wanted to have a different kind of relationship with them than always keeping them off balance.
sentences.zh: 我想和他们建立一种不同类型的关系，而不是总是让他们处于不知所措的状态。

sentences.en: So after I went on to become a clinical psychologist, and in my role, I try to help other people have generous interpretations about themselves and others.
sentences.zh: 所以在成为一名临床心理学家之后，在我的角色中，我努力帮助其他人对自己和他人有宽容的解读。

sentences.en: And I've also made a career out of training physicians to do that.
sentences.zh: 我也把培训医生这样做作为我的职业。

sentences.en: And I really am so grateful that I made that shift in my life.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激我在生活中做出了那个转变。

sentences.en: And I really owe it to Holly.
sentences.zh: 我真的要感谢霍莉。

sentences.en: And I think back to that time so many years ago, and when she cared enough to say something to me, something that probably wasn't easy to say,
sentences.zh: 每当我回想起多年前的那个时刻，当她足够关心我对我说些什么的时候，那番话可能并不容易说出口，

sentences.en: but it was something that changed the direction of my life in a very significant and very gratifying way.
sentences.zh: 但它却以一种非常显著且非常令人欣慰的方式改变了我人生的方向。

sentences.en: So, thank you, Holly.
sentences.zh: 所以，谢谢你，霍莉。

sentences.en: You're my unsung hero.
sentences.zh: 你就是我的无名英雄。
